text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

After appointing his son Lachlan as managing director of News Corp's Australian arm in September and elevating him to the board of directors, Rupert Murdoch has shed more responsibility for the day-to-day operations of his global media empire by appointing two joint chief operating officers, Fox Filmed Entertainment head Peter Chernin and Fox Television head Chase Carey. Page 1.

A survey conducted by Australian Farm Journal magazine has found that two life insurance groups, the AMP Society and National Mutual, are Australia's biggest farmers. AMP's Stanbroke Pastoral Company was the nation's biggest cattle producer this year, with 27 properties in Queensland and the Northern Territory and 350,000 head of cattle. National Mutual remained the biggest wool producer with 300,000 sheep. Page 3.

Despite reporting a net profit of A$197 million after abnormals for the 12 months to September, down from A$269 million a year earlier, plastics, chemicals and explosives group ICI Australia is hoping the benefits of last year's A$350 million capital expenditure and prouctivity programmes will help it recover. Page 23.

It is understood that four bidders, Lend Lease, AMP Investments, the ANZ Bank and Commonwealth Bank Financial Services, are left in the race for Commonwealth Funds Management. Binding bids for the funds manager are to be submitted to the federal government by late November. Page 23.

Unlisted biomedical research group AMRAD Corp yesterday announced a A$70 million initial public offering, in a deal which offers 36 million shares at A$1.95 a share, taking the group's market capitalisation to A$217.5 million. The group was founded in 1986 by four leading Victorian medical research institutes with A$15 million from the former Labor state government. Page 23.

Turning around the losses of last financial year, food group Burns Philp & Co Ltd yesterday announced a first quarter net profit of A$17.6 million, up 42 percent on the same period last year. Earnings before interest, tax and abnormals increased by five percent to A$33.2 million. Page 25.
THE AUSTRALIAN

News Corp Ltd has reshuffled its senior staff in a move which sees the two heads of its United States-based Fox film and TV operations named as co-chief executives of operations of the world-wide media group. Peter Chernin and Chase Carey are now second in charge after chairman and chief executive Rupert Murdoch. Page 23.

Major insurer NRMA Ltd came under the spotlight when current president Don Mackay and five others from the pro-float camp fought off an attempt to dump them from the board, winning strong support from proxy votes to remain at a fiery meeting of NRMA members. Page 23.

St George Bank Ltd's proposed A$2.6 billion takeover of Advance Bank Ltd has recieved a substantial boost from ratings agency Standard & Poor's, which said it would raise St George Bank's current A minus rating to A once the merger was completed. A ratings upgrade could mean a significant savings in funding costs for the merged bank. Page 24.

Chemicals and plastics giant ICI Australia Ltd yesterday reported an 18 percent fall in annual net profit to A$220 million. ICI almost said it would begin on a A$100 million investment drive into Asia to offset the poor performance in its plastics and consumer products division. Page 25.

Tax Commissioner Michael Carmody has called for action to grapple with tax on dealings over the Internet. Speaking at an international business tax conference in Sydney, Carmody urged for the establishment of consistently applied tax principles and discussed the general problems of tax evasion. Page 25.

At Great Central Mines' annual meeting in Melbourne yesterday, chairman Joseph Gutnick told shareholders GCM was looking at developing an underground operation in the new Barton Deeps deposit at the 240,000-ounce-a-year Jundee mine in Western Australia. He said the company was examining doubling the capacity of the processing plant from its rated two million tonnes a year to four million tonnes a year. Page 25.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Battling a barrage of criticism about Coles Myer managing director Peter Bartels' salary package, chairman Nobby Clark claimed yesterday that although the group's annual report said Bartels' pay had risen from A$1.64 million to A$2.87 million in the lates year, his basic salary had remained at A$1.6 million, the amount agreed to when he joined the retailer in 1992. Page 25.

Rupert Murdoch yesterday announced the promotion of two senior U.S. executives, Fox Filmed Entertainment chairman Peter Chernin and Fox Television chairman Chase Carey, to oversee News Corporation's global assets and the appointment of Chernin, Carey and Murdoch's son Lachlan to the board. Page 25.

The Internet web site recently voted as the most popular in a people's choice award, has been forced to close down after the Australian Securities Commission insisted the operator of the site get a dealer's licence. To obtain a licence, Gerry Pauley had to have A$20,000 deposited as security with a bank and would have had to pay about A$270 in application and lodging fees. Page 25.

Australian Taxation Commissioner Michael Carmody has warned an APEC-OECD symposium on international business taxation that the world faces "an electronic black economy blacker than the existing black economy". Carmody said globalisation and technological change could create a company with a A$2 billion profit operating in 20 countries that traded over the Internet in anything that could be digitalised. Page 27.

Addressing yesterday's annual general meeting, Ridley Corp chairman John Keniry said although the salt and grain group's A$95 million bid for Joe White Maltings had secured about 18 percent, it was unlikely to deliver control of the maltster. Ridley managing director Gary Busenshut said the group was still keen to make a major acquisition of up to A$100 million. Page 27.

Following the savaging of the profitability of Australia's three cigarette producers Rothmans, WD & HO Wills and Philip Morris by a severe price discounting war last year, Rothmans said yesterday its interim result would be significantly higher than last year's first half. Page 27.
THE AGE

Following criticism from many quarters, including Federal Shadow Treasurer Gareth Evans and Melbourne businessman John Elliott, Coles Myer yesterday defended the A$2.87 million pay package of its managing director and chief executive, Peter Bartels, with Coles chairman Nobby Clark saying Bartels' basic package had not changed since he started with the company four years ago. Page B1.

Although three groups have submitted proposals for all of the Melbourne Docklands five sites Docklands Authority chief executive John Tabart said the bids would be assessed on a prcinct-by-precinct basis. Twenty groups have been short-listed to develop the area, with giant Japanese construction group Obayashi Corporation and Malaysian developer Gasing Heights leading the Asian push. Page B1.

Ten years after receiving capital of A$14 million from the Victoria Investment Corporation under the former state Labor government's industry development scheme, Amrad Corp yesterday announced plans to raise A$70 million in a float. Page B1.

Part two of Mintel's survey of Australia's A$2 billion cold, non-alcoholic drinks market, has revealed that a new type of consumer, labelled SMART - selective, mobile, adult, rich and thirsty - is prepared to pay a 57 percent premium for drinks such as Sorts Plus, Gatorade, hybrid fruit drinks, iced teas and still water. Page B2.

Australian Taxation Commissioner Michael Carmody predicted a future in which services delivered over the Internet could become virtually tax-free, gaining an unfair advantage over land-based competitors and destroying nations' revenue bases. He made the comments in his opening address to a joint OPEC-OECD symposium on international business taxation in Sydney. Page B3.

Joe White shareholders yesterday rejected Ridley Corporation's bid for two seats on the board to reflect its 18 percent holding, with Joe White chairman S.E.K. Hulme saying it was ludicrous that Ridley should try to seek board representation while it still had a A$5.30 cash takeover bid on the table. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
